host: mol-metal dev host (32 CPU cores, 2 GPUs; other workflows run concurrently)
derivation: Hw = max(standalone MAX, contended wall inside a real --pipeline all --strict pre-flight run, the pre-flight's own cut-off wall in the Wf-A133 baseline run); R = ceil_0.05(max over smokes of Hw/Cw) = the MEASURED worst-case run-to-run inflation; budget = ceil_0.1(Hw * R); headroom_factor = budget / standalone_baseline.
note: MEASURED standalone baselines for the three AGENTS.md 5.7 wire-in smokes, CPU-only (CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=""), full-subprocess wall clock. The module molmetal/scripts/wfa135_smoke_budget.py is the ONE source of truth for the budgets; this fixture is its machine-readable mirror and the regression test asserts the two agree.

p1_chemprop_smoke.note: Hw = 94.8 s is a LOWER BOUND (the Wf-A133 baseline run cut the smoke off at its 90 s budget after 94.8 s). Standalone repeats 1-2 were measured while a concurrent Wf-A135 D-MPNN measurement shared the host; repeats 3-5 were measured with no Wf-A135 job of ours in flight. The MAX over repeats (81.516 s) is used as the baseline, so the budget is conservative by construction.

p3_dmpnn_loss_wire_in_smoke.note: Hw = 300.0 s is a LOWER BOUND (the Wf-A133 baseline run cut the smoke off at its 300 s budget, rc=124). This smoke showed the LARGEST run-to-run spread of the three (215.6 s completed vs >300 s cut off), which is what sets the global R = 1.45.

p3_wf385_scaffold_loss_wire_in_verified.note: The standalone repeat 1 (223.832 s) is the worst observation of this smoke on this host and binds over both the contended wall (159.6 s) and the Wf-A133 baseline run's 150 s INNER cut-off. The budget is the OUTER subprocess budget; the inner gate script is given budget - 30 s so it can still write gate_result.json.
